description:
Location: `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:601`

  let invite = invites
      .into_iter()
      .find(|inv| inv.code == code)
      .ok_or_else(|| JmapError::invalid_arguments("invite code not found"))?;

CONCERN
`inv.code` is the SpaceInvite code field (`crate-jmap-chat-types/src/space.rs:96`), doc'd in the ChatBackend trait (`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:74-89`) as the output of a CSPRNG and explicitly described as 'unguessable'. It is the credential that authorizes a Space/join.

The `String == String` comparison short-circuits at the first mismatched byte. An attacker who can issue Space/join requests can mount a timing oracle to recover an invite code byte-by-byte. The threat is bounded but real: network jitter raises the noise floor but does not eliminate the side-channel for short fixed-length tokens. Industry standard is constant-time compare for any 'is this token correct' check regardless of jitter (NIST SP 800-57, IRTF CFRG guidance).

WHAT GOES WRONG
Key recovery — specifically, invite-code recovery → unauthorized Space membership.

WORKSPACE GAP
`subtle::ConstantTimeEq` is not in the workspace dependency tree (grep confirms zero hits for `subtle::`, `ConstantTimeEq`, `constant_time` across all 25 crates). There is no constant-time-compare facility for future MAC/session-token/HMAC comparisons either.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add `subtle` to workspace.dependencies.
2. In space.rs:601, replace `inv.code == code` with subtle-based compare:
       use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
       inv.code.as_bytes().ct_eq(code.as_bytes()).into()
   (Note: `==` lengths first, then constant-time over the canonical byte length. The two strings can be of different lengths in principle; document the length-discrimination decision.)
3. Document the constant-time invariant on `SpaceInvite.code` in jmap-chat-types and on the trait method that consumes it.

ORACLE
- IRTF CFRG side-channel-resistance guidance for token comparisons (https://datatracker.ietf.org/wg/cfrg/charter/)
- `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` docs (https://docs.rs/subtle)
- Match shape to BearerAuth's existing redaction discipline (auth.rs:183-189) — the workspace already treats credential comparisons as a defended surface elsewhere.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P2. Live exploitable timing oracle on a credential comparison, mitigated only by network jitter. The fix is mechanical and cheap; not blocking publish but should land before crates.io release.
title: Security: non-constant-time invite-code compare in Space/join (crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:601)
